text: Read /home/user/poker-club-app/mcp/heldout/AUTHOR_PROMPT.md and carry out exactly what it says. That file is your complete brief.

1	You are the AUTHOR of a held-out evaluation set. You have no other role in this study: a different agent will answer your questions and code will grade them. Work carefully; your expected answers are the ground truth.
2	
3	## The study
4	A poker league app (two bar venues, "Tight End" on Tuesdays and "Wild Corgi" on Thursdays, two tournament games a night) exposes its league data to AI agents through a read-only MCP server. The question being tested: how reliably does an agent retrieve correct answers from league data through these tools, including knowing when NOT to answer?
5	
6	All data is fictional demo data. Never write real people's names, emails or phone numbers; use only names that appear in the demo fixtures, or obviously invented ones for unknown-name cases.
7	
8	## The data (ground truth)
9	Repository: /home/user/poker-club-app
10	- `demo/fixtures/*.json`: the whole club (players, seasons, schedule, checkins, eliminations, bounties, rsvps, champ_overrides, ...). `demo/seed.js` generated it.
11	- League rules live in the app code: `functions/index.js` (`computeLeaderboard`, `BONUS_POINTS`, `calculateTiePoints`, how standings are ranked and tie-broken, which events count), `public/clock-structures.js` (blind levels), `public/champ-seating.js` (championship-night seating). `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root describes the scoring model.
12	- The system under test treats "today" as 10/20/2026 (this decides each venue's "current season").
13	
14	Compute every expected answer yourself from the fixtures and those rules. Write your scripts in <scratch>/author/ (outside the repository; they will be published only after answering is over).
15	
16	DO NOT read anything under `mcp/` except `mcp/heldout/` (your output folder) and `mcp/eval/heldout-rules.js` + `mcp/eval/heldout-check.js` (the grading contract). In particular do not read `mcp/lib`, `mcp/eval/questions.jsonl`, `mcp/eval/oracle.js`, `mcp/eval/build-questions.js`, `mcp/eval/results`, `mcp/test`, or `mcp/README.md`; that is the system under test and an earlier, separate question set. Do not run the MCP server or `mcp/eval/call.js`: gold must not come from the system being tested.
17	
18	## The tools the answerer will have (descriptions only)
19	1. `get_season_standings(venue, season?, limit?)`: ranked season standings for one venue, computed the way the league leaderboard computes them; each row has rank, tied flag, points, games played, wins, bounties, RSVPs honored, berth. Also the season window and any unfinalized games already counted. Errors: unknown_venue, unknown_season.
20	2. `get_player_season_history(player, venue?, season?)`: one player's season totals (rank, points, games, wins, bounties, best finish) and every game with finish, points and bounties. Names match exactly after trimming/lowercasing/collapsing spaces, or by a roster alias; nothing is guessed. Omit venue for both venues. Errors: unknown_player (with suggestions), ambiguous_player, unknown_venue, unknown_season.
21	3. `get_game_seating(venue, date, game)`: who played one game. Regular nights: the field in check-in order with finishes, and the final table (seat numbers are drawn at the table and NOT recorded). Championship nights: the director's seating chart (playing, cleared, onDeck, consolation, consolationWaitlist, out). Errors: unknown_venue, invalid_date, no_game, game_not_played.
22	4. `get_game_structure(venue?, date?)`: blind levels (minutes, start minute, blinds, breaks, chip-ups), the points table, tie and attendance rules, championship seating rules; with venue and date, the event type that night and whether it counts toward the season. Errors: unknown_venue, invalid_date, no_game.
23	Venue and season are optional where marked; season accepts a name like "Fall 2026" or a number.
24	
25	The tools do NOT expose: emails, phone numbers, drink/shot orders, RSVPs as a list, seat numbers on regular nights, announcements, anything about the future beyond the schedule's event type.
26	
27	## What to [cut]
